queue_rollup.decision: The receive-queue change stayed out of the checkout. At the device’s four-Call capacity, the synchronous GET slowed in seven of eight local pairs and async deferred completion slowed in all eight. Larger Call tables benefited. In the matched Windows release runs, 4 KiB OSCORE throughput rose 0.5% in six of six pairs with equal median charged server CPU. Unprotected 4 KiB median throughput fell 1.4% and its p99 rose from 101.8 to 107.8 µs. Both experimental binaries used the same fixed source directory, lock, fixture and release profile. The separately rebuilt control has a different text section from the retained release, so comparisons stay within the pair.

differences: AES 0.9.3 in original and 0.9.4 in current, selected by each project manifest.
The Coaptic I/O procedural macro uses Syn 2.0.119 in original and Syn 3.0.9 in current at compile time.

method.release: Single-thread Tokio release server with bounded AllocMemory and a verifying native client. One outstanding confirmable read, 32 warmups; single datagram for 64 B and four for 4096 B. Established OSCORE setup is outside measurement. Same runtime, capacities, arrival rate, security and client across compared server arms.
method.counter_units: sCPU and cCPU are gated process user+kernel microseconds/verified read; sCycles and cCycles are cycles/read. Latency p50/p99 microseconds. Rate reads/second. sWS,cWS,sPB,cPB and peak working set in MiB. sApp and sFuture are bytes and account for different owners. Medians of individual windows.

server_capacity.body_bytes: representation rounded up to the next 1024 bytes

method.design: Three-arm runs cover all six permutations, reversing workload order on alternate rounds. Final paced runs alternate original/final and final/original for four rounds. Each window launches fresh processes. Separate state snapshots and inclusive stack samples are wall-time observations of the event-loop thread; charged process CPU comes only from profiler-off windows. Same-host loopback and OS clock granularity limit interpretation of small absolute differences.
method.code_path: A fresh process per arm per mode, six order-balanced rounds at fixed host affinity, first in-process traversal discarded. codec/decode validates then iterates a multi-option upload packet, codec/encode writes a two-path two-query GET. Upload uses eight 16-byte fragments of one 128-byte PUT. Q delivers NUM1 before NUM0. The fixed and allocated Engine probes verify assembled bytes, release and reuse; App classic also verifies the handler input, every MID, response code and final body. Timings are elapsed ns per complete operation excluding fixture setup. Local memory fields report the actual Rust object size, not stack high-water or heap.
method.device: Admission comparison uses 4/arm matched seeds, 8 reads per path/preference per boot; 512 verified reads plus identity checks. CPU comparison uses 2/arm/meter state, 24 native verified operations per boot. Task samples pair receive return and send return by MID and length, including IRQ time charged to the worker. Free heap and stack readings have different coverage from Windows process memory. The C service lacks the matched durable OSCORE endpoint.

candidate_names.final: combined including upload binding and refusal fix

method.workload_fields: The per-workload heap, scratch, pending Call metadata and RX-body fields come from the native verifying client. server_capacity describes the independently constructed server. Its UDP adapter reserves 2049 scratch bytes. sWS and sPB are end-of-window process readings; sPeakWS is lifetime peak and may include startup. The corresponding c-prefixed values belong to the client.
